summary: Allocates a 108-byte view/projection structure, initializes it with ViewProjectionStructInit, then allocates a 12-byte linked-list node holding it and inserts the node at the tail of the list rooted at this. The insertion is gated on the enable flag at this+0x88 and on a2 being non-null. When the list is empty (head this+0x8 is null) the node becomes both head this+0x8 and first-reference this+0x10; otherwise it links after the current tail this+0xC. The tail is advanced to the new node and the count at this+0x14 is incremented. The initialized 108-byte structure is returned even when the 12-byte node allocation fails.

local_names.this: list owner: enable flag at +0x88, head at +0x8, tail at +0xC, first-reference at +0x10, count at +0x14
local_names.a2: context parameter forwarded to ViewProjectionStructInit; also a hard gate (null returns 0)
local_names.v6: initialized 108-byte view/projection structure, the function return value

operations.description: Returns 0 immediately when the enable flag at this+0x88 (this[34]) is zero
Returns 0 immediately when a2 is null
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(108) allocates the 108-byte structure; a null result also returns 0
ViewProjectionStructInit initializes the 108-byte structure with (v5, a2, a3, a4, this); a null result returns 0
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12) allocates the node; on success it is initialized to [0]=v6, [4]=0, [8]=0, otherwise the node pointer is nulled
If the head at this+0x8 (this[2]) is non-null, the old tail's next at this+0xC+4 is set to the new node; otherwise the node becomes both head this+0x8 and first-reference this+0x10
The tail pointer this+0xC (this[3]) is advanced to the new node
The node count at this+0x14 (this[5]) is incremented
Returns v6, the initialized 108-byte structure, regardless of whether the node allocation succeeded

clean_pseudocode: v6 = ViewProjectionStructInit(v5, a2, a3, a4, this);
if (this[2]) { *(void**)(this[3]+4) = v7; } else { this[2] = v7; this[4] = v7; }
